parked.title: try/catch on phUSD.mint catches out-of-gas under the 63/64 rule, so a gas-starved call could force banking on an otherwise-successful mint
parked.reason: CONFIDENCE != SEVERITY. Confidence that the pattern APPLIES is low; the reason it is parked rather than dropped is its COMPOSITION with DEDUP-11-001: if it applies, it removes DEDUP-11-001's mint-authority-outage precondition entirely, converting a triple-gated Low into something reachable without any owner action. That is a severity-relevant composition, so it does not get dropped on a low-confidence-of-applicability basis (Law 1).

refutedBy.argument: The griefing window requires cost(mint) > 63 x cost(catch), and it is not close. `try` forwards 63/64 of gas and retains 1/64. The catch is two SSTOREs plus an event: unclaimablePhUSDOf cold zero->nonzero (~22.1k) + totalUnclaimablePhUSD cold nonzero->nonzero (~7.1k) + PhUSDMintFailed (~1.5k) = ~31k. An ERC20 mint is ~50k. Requiring 1/64*G >= 31k forces G >= ~1.98M, which forwards ~1.95M to the mint — roughly 39x more than it needs. The two conditions are mutually exclusive by a ~40x margin. The same arithmetic refutes the nested variant on MigratorV2V3.migrate -> migrateOne -> stake -> mint.

REACHABILITY: all three _claimRewards call sites are auth-gated by `require(msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator)` (:697/:741/:791). A third party cannot reach ANOTHER user's claim path at all, so the 63/64 vector has no third-party entry point. INCENTIVE: on self-service paths beneficiary == msg.sender == the victim, so 'forcing the bank' means banking one's OWN value — strictly negative EV. HARM: even if forced, the loss is DEFERRAL not destruction; the bank is pullable.
refutedBy.pocEvidence: test_ECON005_thirdPartyCannotForceVictimBank — PASS. Bob (unprivileged) is rejected with 'Not authorized' on claim(alice), withdraw(1 ether, alice), and stake(1 ether, alice).

parked.residualQuestionNotFullyClosed: Both refutations are strong and largely close this. The residual the parking exists for: econ-scanner's refutation addresses THIRD-PARTY griefing (the migrator is a trusted owner-set delegate, so it is excluded under Law 3), and code-scanner's arithmetic addresses the gas margin. Neither directly PoC's the MIGRATOR-SELF composition: an owner running a poorly-metered migrate(maxIterations) pass, where migrate -> `try this.migrateOne(...)` -> stake -> `try phUSD.mint(...)` nests THREE 63/64 boundaries. Code-scanner asserts the same ~40x arithmetic covers it and notes migrateOne's own docstring already flags the 63/64 hazard (backstopped by owner-only skipCurrent) — that is likely correct and no counter-evidence exists. Parked at LOW priority for a cheap gas-metering check, not because the refutation is doubted.
parked.confidenceInRefutation: high — two independent agents, one with a passing PoC, one with quantitative arithmetic. This is close to droppable; it is parked only because of the DEDUP-11-001 composition.
parked.routingReason: Below the emit threshold (two independent refutations, one PoC-backed) but composes with an emitted finding in a way that would change that finding's gating. Parked visibly per Law 1 rather than dropped.
parked.suggestedAction: Optional: a gas-metering PoC on the nested migrate -> migrateOne -> stake -> mint path. If it confirms code-scanner's arithmetic, close this outright and record the closure against DEDUP-11-001's escalationTriggers.

parked.title: startPromotion (:399/:401) and topUpPromotion (:424/:426) are onlyOwner with NO nonReentrant and commit promo state AFTER an external transfer of an owner-chosen token

verifiedFromSource.startPromotion: `function startPromotion(address token, uint256 amount, uint256 duration) external onlyOwner whenNotPaused {` (:389) — no nonReentrant. Order: require(promoPhase == None) (:390) -> _updatePool() (:398) -> IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, amount) (EXTERNAL CALL) -> promoToken/promoRewardBalance/promoDepletionDuration/promoRewardPerSecond/promoPhase = Active (:403-407).
verifiedFromSource.topUpPromotion: `function topUpPromotion(uint256 amount) external onlyOwner {` (:417) — no nonReentrant. Order: require(promoPhase == Active) -> _updatePool() -> promoToken.safeTransferFrom (EXTERNAL CALL) -> promoRewardBalance += amount; promoRewardPerSecond = ... (:428-429).

whatIsRefuted: DIRECT RE-ENTRY INTO THESE FUNCTIONS IS BLOCKED BY onlyOwner. The tempting shape — a reentrant startPromotion passing the `promoPhase == None` check because the phase is not committed until AFTER the transfer, letting a second promotion be started and then silently overwritten by the outer frame (promoRewardBalance is assigned `=`, not `+=`, so the inner token's amount would be stranded) — is UNREACHABLE: a callback from a hooked token arrives with msg.sender == the token contract, which fails onlyOwner. Only the owner can re-enter, and a malicious owner is out of scope (Law 3).

RETRO-ACCRUAL IS BLOCKED. _updatePool() runs BEFORE the external call and before promoToken is assigned, so lastRewardTime == now when the promo slot is populated. This is V3-H-01's fix property and it is CONFIRMED STILL INTACT: 'startPromotion calls _updatePool() BEFORE assigning promoToken and finalizePromotion zeroes it, so a stale lastRewardTime spanning a flush window cannot retro-accrue against the NEXT promo token — the most plausible reintroduction path, closed.' Nothing moves lastRewardTime backwards.

REENTERING PERMISSIONLESS FUNCTIONS DURING THE WINDOW LOOKS BENIGN. At the moment of startPromotion's transferFrom: _updatePool has run, promoToken is NOT yet set, promoPhase == None, and promoRewardPerSecond is 0 (finalizePromotion zeroes it). A reentrant stake would accrue no promo and would simply be a stake placed before the promo started — correct behaviour, not a defect.
parked.whyNotDropped: Because no contract-wide lock is held during the external call, the permissionless nonReentrant set (stake/withdraw/claim/batchClaim/collectReward) IS re-enterable from inside an owner call. That is structurally the SAME shape as ledger entry V3-Q-04 (81c3d77d, open, qa) — whose reachable-set enumeration came back clean and whose doNotEscalate I respect. BUT that enumeration was performed for finalizePromotion SPECIFICALLY, and these two functions have a materially different check-then-act shape (`promoPhase == None` / `== Active` checked before the external call and committed after it, versus finalizePromotion's `== Flushing`). I will not claim V3-Q-04's clean enumeration covers functions it was not run on. My own walk above found nothing harmful, but it is a single-agent walk, not the full enumeration V3-Q-04 got.
parked.law3Note: Law 3 IS reached here (unlike the 8 migrator hits, which are refuted by the nonReentrant guard itself). Reaching this at all requires the owner to select a hooked/ERC777-class promo token — which is exactly the precondition of emitted finding DEDUP-11-004, filed at Low. This is likely owner-trust noise. It is not blanket-dropped because the task explicitly required per-hit adjudication given this project's V3-H-01 promo-phase history, and because the honest answer is 'my walk found nothing' rather than 'the enumeration cleared it'.

parked.reason: Re-derived from source this run (econ-scanner, NOT auto-suppressed and NOT deferred to the cached entry — which matters, because KI-based suppression is BLOCKED this run). Both suppression legs re-verified independently, one empirically. LEG 1 (SolvencyDetermination.md 2: phUSD minted on demand, no pre-funded pool, solvency == active mint privilege — DOCUMENTED DESIGN) holds. LEG 2 (TRIGGER-NOT-FIRED: desiredAPYBps has no constructor initializer => 0 by construction) holds, re-verified at src/PhlimboV3.sol:60 (line drifted 63 -> 60 since run-08; the property is unchanged) and proven empirically by test_ECON004_atShippedZeroAPY_bankIsUnreachable (a fresh PhlimboV3 at the shipped config, warped 10 years, yields pendingPhUSD == 0; with the mint forced to revert, claim() writes NOTHING to the bank).

doesStory031WidenTheSurface.verdict: NO — the bank is a STRICT SUBSET of the stream DEDUP-04 already governs, and cannot exceed it.
argument: MAGNITUDE: the catch at :915 banks `pendingPhUSDAmount` — bit-for-bit the same value the success path would have minted at :913. It authorizes no wei that accPhUSDPerShare had not already accrued. banked + paid == earned exactly (proven: test_ECON003).

DORMANCY: the mint leg is guarded by `if (pendingPhUSDAmount > 0)` (:903). At desiredAPYBps == 0, pending is identically zero, the leg is never entered, and the bank is never written. The bank is dormant for EXACTLY the same reason, under exactly the same condition, as DEDUP-04 itself. LEG 2 covers the bank with no gap.

LEG 1 CONSISTENCY: the bank is an IOU redeemable if-and-only-if mint privilege is active (a failed pull reverts and leaves the bank intact, :649). That is a literal restatement of 'solvency == active mint privilege', not a departure from it.

NO NEW DEFERRAL POWER: retroactive-mint-on-authority-restore already existed BEFORE story-031 via `pending` — _updatePool advances accPhUSDPerShare regardless of mint authority, so under the old code a user held un-claimable pending across the outage and claimed the full backlog on restore. story-031 changes WHERE the crystallized amount is recorded (bank vs pending), not WHETHER it is retroactively mintable. Economically neutral.

parked.title: A wont-fix entry (V3-M-07) was fixed anyway one day after triage, and wont-fix entries are not normally rescanned — the closure would have gone undetected outside a diff-anchored run
parked.detail: V3-M-07 (27e83ab2) was human-triaged WONT-FIX on 2026-07-16 under Law-3 owner-trust reasoning ('a self-inflicted cutting off nose to spite the face action — at worst a temporary, owner-reversible misconfiguration'). On 2026-07-17, story-031 implemented V3-M-07's recommendation VERBATIM. This run detected the closure only because it was diff-anchored on story-031 and V3-M-07 sits in the diff. Had story-031 touched a different file, the ledger would now carry a permanently stale wont-fix on code that no longer has the defect.
parked.whyItMatters: Two distinct hazards, both Law-1-adjacent. (1) STALE-STATUS: a wont-fix that is silently fixed leaves the ledger describing code that no longer exists, which corrodes trust in every other wont-fix. (2) INVALIDATED RATIONALE: more seriously, V3-M-07's wont-fix rationale ('Fully recoverable — re-grant mint role or emergencyTransfer') is the exact property that story-031 BROKE on the migrator leg. The banked phUSD is now recoverable by NEITHER mechanism. A wont-fix precedent whose load-bearing property has been invalidated by a later change is a live suppression risk: a future run could reasonably reach for V3-M-07 as grounds to suppress DEDUP-11-001, and would be wrong. That is why DEDUP-11-001 carries a mandatory ledgerDisclosure block naming this explicitly.
parked.routingReason: Not a code finding, so it does not belong in deduplicated-findings.json's findings[]. But it is exactly the kind of process gap that lets a real issue slip, so it goes in the visible channel rather than a run note nobody re-reads.
suggestedAction: Apply the V3-M-07 propose-fixed (see deduplicated-findings.json ledgerReconciliation).

Consider whether wont-fix entries need a detection path for 'recommendation was later implemented' — e.g. include wont-fix entries in the fix-verification sweep when their contract:function appears in a diff, even though they are excluded from re-reporting.

Consider whether a wont-fix whose stated rationale is later invalidated by a code change should auto-surface for re-triage. V3-M-07 is a clean worked example: the rationale rested on 'fully recoverable', and the fix removed the recoverability on one leg.
